Q: When "Antigravity" sidebar view for Dev Container is broken, how to open a container in it? A:

I guess you're using VS Code with Remote - SSH. I encountered the exact same issue and digged into the logs. The root cause is a bug in Antigravity's built-in Dev Containers extension when handling nested remote workspace URIs (specifically SSH).

If you look at the Output channel for the "Dev Containers" extension, you'll likely see a stack trace similar to this:

[Error - 09:42:15.981] Failed to get Dev Container workspace information:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'endsWith')
    at n.parse (.../extensions/antigravity-dev-containers/dist/extension.js:...)
    at n.parseAuthority (.../extensions/antigravity-dev-containers/dist/extension.js:...)

Explanation

This TypeError occurs in the parseAuthority function. It seems the extension tries to parse the current window's URI authority to determine the workspace context. However, when you are already connected to a remote server via SSH (a "Remote - SSH" session), the URI authority differs from what the extension expects (e.g., local file scheme vs. SSH remote scheme).

The extension fails to handle this specific remote authority format, leading to an undefined value where it expects a string, causing the crash when it attempts to call .endsWith() on it. Consequently, the extension backend dies, resulting in the "There is no data provider registered" message in the UI.

Workaround

Since the UI integration is broken for this specific nested scenario (SSH -> Docker), you can manually perform the equivalent operations in the integrated terminal:

  1. Build your image manually:
docker build -t my-dev-container .devcontainer/
  1. Run the container interactively: Mount your current remote directory into the container to compile or run tests:
docker run --rm -it -v $(pwd):/workspaces/project -w /workspaces/project my-dev-container bash

This confirms that your .devcontainer configuration files are correct and will work for other collaborators using standard VS Code, even if the plugin UI in Antigravity is currently bugged.

Q: Running Docker container fails due to dotnet-isolated not found A:

This usually happens when the container image doesn’t include the .NET isolated worker, even though your app is configured to use it.

Azure hides this because it provides the runtime for you, but locally your container must include it explicitly.

Most of the time the cause is the wrong base image in the Dockerfile.

For .NET 8 isolated Functions, the base image should be something like:

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/azure-functions/dotnet-isolated:4-dotnet-isolated8

If you’re using a generic .NET / ASP.NET image, or an older Azure Functions image, the host starts but can’t find the dotnet-isolated worker, which leads to:

WorkerConfig for runtime: "dotnet-isolated" not found

FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME=dotnet-isolated is correct — changing it won’t fix the issue.

Also, this has nothing to do with docker vs docker-compose; both will fail the same way if the image is missing the worker.

Once the final stage of your Dockerfile uses the correct Azure Functions .NET 8 isolated base image, the container should start normally.

Q: Keycloak and new organization feature with multi membership on a user ( v26 ) A:

In 26.4, after starting the instance with dynamic-scopes feature flag, you must enable dynamic scope for organization and will work as expected. The effects are:
- If identity provider is set up, organization claim will contain an array with all organizations the user is member of. The oidc client must be organization:*
- If no identity provider is set up, login with user/pass

  • if dynamic scope is off, the user is prompted to select an org at login (and the scope requested by the oidc client must be just organization
  • if dynamic scope is on, the user is NOT prompted, organization claim will contain array of all orgs, and you must use organization:* scope in the client
